summary.title: Build Your Own Text Editor
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a working minimal text editor in C, step by step, by typing in about 184 code changes to a version of antirez's kilo.
keywords: build a text editor in c
takeaways: Build a roughly 1000-line single-file text editor in C with no dependencies, by following 184 steps
Enter terminal raw mode and handle raw input and output
Build a text viewer and then extend it into a text editor
Add search and syntax highlighting features to the editor
summary.summary: This is a step-by-step tutorial booklet that walks the reader through building a minimal text editor in C. The editor is based on antirez's kilo, with some changes, and is described as about 1000 lines in one file with no dependencies. The booklet has 184 steps, each adding, changing, or removing a few lines, with compile-and-run checkpoints along the way. Chapters cover setup, raw mode, a text viewer, a text editor, search, and syntax highlighting, with appendices for help.
